column5: How to read: builds to implementation depth the base's hook-depth built-in clerk of item 101 (d) (staged 'after the API'), plus the tool API parts the base names and never types — the oracle's answer, the reader's map brief, the solver's explanation — and the host clerk seam; the implementer holds the base and this volume only (§17.1); base facts cited never restated; base changes filed as BCR-V10-n (§10), volume written as if applied; decisions J-V10.n (§9), tests T-V10-n (§7); unprefixed § = base, V10 §n this volume, V0n §x another volume; item numbers are the owner's amendment items (files c, d, e, g), g items' base mechanisms cited by item.

Plain words, what it is: 'Assistant (AI)' in the program, the clerk in this design; optional helper in a drawer; four things only: reads the map and answers; explains why anything is where it is (with alternatives considered); builds — turns described towns or pasted lists into the same twelve tools; checks a plan before commit.

Plain words, how it feels: nothing changes the map by itself; every suggestion is a ghost with one line saying what and why, counts of plots, households, buildings, anything moved, and up to three versions; accept, try again or drop; an accepted suggestion is one undo step; follow-ups ('make the lower city denser') are new suggestions; where a rule says no (fixed by SettlementForge or locked) it says so and offers the nearest possible things as buttons.

Plain words, item 110: proposes viaducts, aqueducts on arches, terraces, a fort at a mole's head, stepped tiers exactly as the canvas tools would; explains a generated raised way's reason ('it crosses the gorge, a 34 m drop') and absences ('a town builds them only once it is a city; you may draw one'); before a removal shows every consequence ('the road goes round by the lower bridge; the fountain on the square loses its water'); once accepted the town never builds it back; 'put it back' returns it; never adds a raised way, terrace or retaining wall and never removes anything unless asked.

Plain words, what it never does: never draws a picture — writes only the tools' declarations (movable, reshapable, re-rollable; exports say which parts were drawn, derived or proposed); never invents SettlementForge facts (places what the dossier lists, never adds, removes or renames); never tells a view what it may not know (a player's assistant sees as the player; a secret guild's name never reaches it; a hidden function behind a shop front does not exist for it); a hidden house is 'a building'; unfound caves and ruins do not exist below the GM; View as limits the assistant too; explains the underground (ways down, sealed caves, crypts vs catacombs, stagnating catacombs); answers history questions and distances ('about 340 m by street'); any SettlementForge claim must come from the map, else greyed 'not found on the map'; 'a village' gives a village once that product is installed.

Plain words, turning it on and cost: off until opened, labelled AI everywhere; 'runs on Claude, Anthropic's model, over the internet: in the standalone program you paste your own Anthropic API key (it stays on your machine), or the program that embeds the map — SettlementForge, say — provides the connection, or uses its own assistant instead'; a question costs a few cents, a building request tens of cents; a monthly limit, the drawer shows spend; settings (model, spend) belong to the device, a shared map never changes them; without the assistant every tool and feature works the same. What leaves the machine: messages and a written description of the map filtered to the view's knowledge (district names, landmarks, roads, walls in words and bearings); never the map file, an image, a withheld secret, or the key to anyone but Anthropic (or the chosen host); conversations in memory unless kept; accepted changes live in the map's history.

Builds (1) @plat/clerk (BCR-V10-8) in two entry points: @plat/clerk/core — everything needing no model: the map brief's text rendering, the spatial resolver, the twelve tools' encoders (tool inputs to §7.1's events), drafts and proposals, variations, the critique engine, the knowledge guard, the grounding check, transcripts and their skeleton projection, the usage meter and settings; @plat/clerk/model — the model backend (ClerkBackend), request builder, streaming turn loop and system prompt, loaded lazily only when the clerk is on (J-V10.2). (2) The model-facing tool set — sixteen tools: the twelve declaration tools of §7.1's toolkit (typed inputs encoding to that tool's events), read_map and why (reader and oracle), check_draft and critique (dry run and rules check); schemas generated from @plat/model's event schemas and @plat/tables' vocabularies so the clerk can never emit an event the canvas cannot (J-V10.5).

Builds (3) the oracle at depth: typed WhyAnswer, per-kind WhyProviders in §2.8's entity registry, the placement solver's read-only explain mode with candidate mode, the prosperity field's driver decomposition (BCR-V10-1..4), open sections so every volume's explainer can add rows, a generic provider for every other kind (BCR-V10-3), the placement's order index (BCR-V10-15); serves the clerk, V09's why panel and any host clerk; carries g items' explanations: item 102 daylight share, 103 (e) rows that pulled, 104 (a) resolution rung, 105 (j) links and goods, 106 (g) unwalled sides, 107 spread vs pull, 108 record members, 109 ruins, ways down, sealed voids, catacombs and crypts (V10 §3.9a), 110 raised ways with recorded reasons, reasons a city built none, a removed thing's removal, retaining walls and deck plots (V10 §3.9). (4) Reader kinds (BCR-V10-1): brief, entity, sites, measure, frame (V06 frames), rule, profile (V11), plus clerk-side reads chronicle and history. (5) Scratch documents (edit mode copy; creation mode fresh generation; BCR-V10-5) and key-filtered dry-run results with created addresses (BCR-V10-6). (6) Preview-first protocol (up to three variations, one undo step, retry, drop, stale) and the apply-then-undo setting (§13.4's fallback).

Builds (7) natural language to a skeleton draft and a roster, iteration, critique rules, refusals with alternatives, never-invent-a-dossier-fact and knowledge gating, transcripts replaying as skeletons; (8) the host clerk seam — three configurations (built-in clerk on the user's key; built-in through a host's proxy; the host's own clerk over the bridge), the bridge messages selecting them, the proposal card a host's own clerk gets and the answer telling it what the user chose, and the words-only projection of every reader answer leaving the frame (BCR-V10-7); (9) cost and latency budgets, offline, safety and privacy, the evaluation set (graders, tiers, pass bars), the command-line clerk plat clerk only if the browser cannot reach the provider (J-V10.24); (10) the drawer's harness ClerkHarness = V09's ClerkHandle (no member of its own), reaching a host's bridge only through ClerkMount.host; (11) item 110's calls: typed forms for retaining walls, terraces, islets, raised ways and aqueducts, deck slots, stepped tiers, span uses (V10 §2.12, §4.1); removal of any generated thing through T10 (BCR-V10-20); anchors inside raw events (J-V10.73); effects shown before apply (V10 §3.11); none declared or removed unasked (V10 §3.3 rule 16); the second known-city fixture's scripted transcript (V10 §3.15).

Clerk state is session and device state, never model state: nothing enters the model digest, records digest, log or document except two base mechanisms: the events a user accepts (proposedBy 'clerk', §7.1, creation prefixes included, BCR-V10-16) and clerk.content rows a document's override layer carries (§7.6), which no model stage reads; every clerk.ops and clerk.content cell carries §1.7's {value, unit, provenance, calibratable}; base records added (reader answers, oracle sections, placement order index) are typed in V10 §2.13 and placed by the BCRs.

@plat/clerk sits after the facade: … ← port ← api ← clerk ← app; imports @plat/api, @plat/model (event schemas, Id, FactTier, Blueprint, MsgRef), @plat/tables (clerk.ops, clerk.content, vocabularies, V09's message catalogue files) and nothing else of plat/; imported by @plat/app (drawer), @plat/testkit (evaluation harness) and, only if spike S1 fails, @plat/cli (plat clerk). Entry points: @plat/clerk/core (model-free: brief renderer, spatial resolver, encoders, drafts, proposals, critique engine, knowledge guard, grounding check, transcripts, usage meter, settings, createClerk(mount); the app uses it without the model, e.g. skeleton critique) and @plat/clerk/model (backend, request builder, prompt, turn loop; a lazily loaded chunk fetched on the first send after switch-on; the provider SDK @anthropic-ai/sdk imported in exactly one adapter file src/backend/anthropic.ts, §14's one-adapter rule, licence row BCR-V10-9).
